Thanks for the heads-up, Jas. High-level legal stance below (quick turnaround):

1) Notice window ladder: we can consider a 30-day notice for Year 1 only if we secure a hard minimum commitment (pro-rated prepayment or non-cancellable minimum) and a strict carveback that prevents notice reduction from applying to any reserved/dedicated capacity. Suggested language: "Notwithstanding Section X, Customer may provide thirty (30) days' prior written notice of non-renewal for the initial twelve (12) month term only; thereafter the parties' standard sixty (60) day notice applies. Any reserved capacity commitments shall remain subject to the original term and fees."

2) Termination for Convenience (TfC): TfC is generally acceptable with constraints. We should limit the scope: no TfC for active migrations, and require a transition plan approved by Redwood. The proposed 10% holdback is workable but we should be explicit on the release triggers (successful data handoff, access termination, final invoice paid). Also cap the holdback duration to 60 days and allow us to set off costs for expedited decommissioning.

3) Escrow / holdback: define calculation (10% of remaining term vs. 10% of last invoice) — recommend 10% of remaining pre-paid fees to avoid surprises.

I'll draft precise redline snippets and share in a follow-up within 2 hours. If procurement wants reduced notice for Year 1, require either: (a) prepayment covering first 3 months, or (b) minimum spend guarantee for Year 1 equal to 50% of the committed TCV.

Karthik

Ellen — thanks, and appreciate the flexibility. Quick internal summary and our proposed compromise below (we'll follow with a redline PDF):

Proposal (summary):
- Notice ladder: 30-day notice permitted for the initial 12 months for month-to-month subscription components only; reserved/dedicated capacity remains under 60-day notice.
- Commercial guardrail: Customer provides a Year 1 minimum-spend guarantee equal to 50% of Year 1 TCV (not necessarily prepaid).
- TfC: Allowed with a 10% holdback, calculated as 10% of the remaining pre-paid fees for the applicable subscription components. Holdback releases: (a) 30 days after Customer completes self-service transition checklist, or (b) 60 days after successful coordinated transition (if Redwood ops performed handoff). We will retain right to set off reasonable decommissioning costs.
